list.title: Document Structure AI — Master's Thesis
list.description: Intelligent document digitisation platform combining DocLayout-YOLO for layout detection and TrOCR/Gemini for OCR, built with FastAPI and React.

detail.description: End-to-end platform that transforms scanned documents and PDFs into clean, editable HTML — faithfully preserving the original layout structure. The system uses a hybrid AI pipeline combining local computer vision (DocLayout-YOLOv10) for layout segmentation and cloud-based LLMs (Gemini) for semantic OCR, ensuring no critical component like signatures, stamps, or tables is lost during reconstruction.

features.title: Drag & drop upload
features.description: Upload scanned notes or PDFs instantly. Supports images and multi-page documents with a single drag-and-drop action.

features.title: AI-powered layout detection
features.description: DocLayout-YOLOv10 analyses the visual structure in real time, detecting headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, logos, signatures, and stamps.

features.title: Semantic HTML reconstruction
features.description: Gemini API transcribes and structures the document into clean, accessible HTML5 — faithfully preserving the original hierarchy and reading order.

features.title: Hybrid reconstruction
features.description: Non-text elements like signatures and stamps are extracted via OpenCV and re-embedded as Data URLs, ensuring nothing is lost.

roadmap.description: Defined the core problem — turning handwritten/scanned notes into structured, editable digital documents. Explored state-of-the-art models for layout detection (DocLayout-YOLO) and OCR (TrOCR, Gemini).
Tested multiple model combinations in a Colab notebook. Compared YOLO variants, evaluated TrOCR vs Gemini for text extraction accuracy, and refined the detection pipeline.
Once the pipeline was stable, integrated it into a FastAPI microservice. Added PDF rasterisation (pdf2image), image normalisation (Pillow/OpenCV), and Gemini structural prompting.
Built a React/Next.js interface with drag-and-drop upload, real-time layout preview, and an editable HTML output panel. Deployed the app on Google Cloud Run.
Presented the full project before the Master's jury — covering the architecture, pipeline decisions, and live demo of the working application.

detail.reflections: Building a generic CV pipeline is harder than it looks — edge cases multiply fast: varying image quality, handwriting vs print, complex multi-column layouts, millions of potential document formats. The model works well within its scope but would need significantly more training data to generalise. After presenting the project, I spoke with fellow students who confirmed how useful a tool like this would be — something close to NotebookLM but with layout-aware digitisation as the core feature. An obvious next step (that I ran out of time to test) is improving handwritten text recognition in the pipeline.

list.title: Azajya — Business Website
list.description: Full-cycle website development from design to deployment, including a CMS for the client to manage their project listings independently.

detail.description: Azajya is a scaffolding and façade cladding company with over 30 years in the market and almost no digital footprint. The client needed a website where people can understand what the company does, and a place where they can upload their projects to showcase them to their clients.

roadmap.description: Working from the existing logo, I'm creating a design that reflects the company's values and branding colours, and building an interactive prototype to present to the client. The project is currently at this stage.
Validate the prototype together with the client, iterate on their feedback, and lock down the final design direction.
Build the frontend from the approved design, with special attention to responsiveness and performance.
Develop the CMS as a standalone backend and integrate it with the frontend, so the client can upload and manage their projects autonomously.
Make sure everything meets the client's expectations and walk them through how to use the CMS to publish their projects.
